note: Acceptance obligations, not executable tests or measured results. S7 cases are follow-on cleanup acceptance.

cases.requirement: open stdin with no input; every operation returns or hits a bounded deadline, never awaits OK.
closed stdin and missing optional configuration; return structured output without a wizard.
a child asks a terminal question; no inherited human input, no automatic `yes`, bounded completion.
large simultaneous stdout/stderr and machine stdin; no unbounded memory or deadlock.
absent credentials never trigger Jacu login, editor, pager or credential UI.
repeated unchanged failure does not consume endless retries; terminal reporting is possible.
external host denial remains external; no permission-mode rewrite.
no default full-suite invocation on every edit.
a filter selects zero tests; it cannot satisfy a behavioral obligation.
interrupted, timed-out or truncated execution cannot pass.
identical reusable state uses the existing successful receipt exactly once.
relevant source, features, toolchain, fixtures, policy or environment change invalidates reuse.
dirty/untracked input change is not hidden by unchanged commit SHA.
changing external state disables ordinary reuse unless explicitly modeled.
simultaneous Jacu requests for the same resource avoid duplicate work; no unrelated process is killed.
stale/concurrently edited candidate cannot approve a newer delivery.
delivery only executes missing/invalidated obligations; no mandatory second full run.
existing smoke/E2E/native output is captured through the same protocol.
"done" text without implementation/evidence returns incomplete.
one omitted original outcome remains visible and outstanding.
self-approved scope reduction or weakened required assertion cannot satisfy closure.
implemented-but-unverified and verified-but-unintegrated are not complete.
a real external blocker returns truthful terminal incomplete without a question.
a valid delivery report references the actual target and all current obligations.
task implementation in another worktree is found before duplicate implementation.
unrelated dirty/active/locked work is preserved and does not block independent delivery.
a reachable historical commit later reverted is not evidence of current behavior.
combined candidate is checked after permitted integration.
missing/inaccessible worktree and stale remote refs are reported, not silently assumed safe.
spaces, non-ASCII, newline-bearing filenames, symlinks and option-like refs are handled safely.
mechanical task maps to focused guidance without a costly extra classifier call.
consequence floor survives a low line count or low difficulty sum.
unsupported/unobservable effort is advisory/null, never falsely applied.
meaningful new evidence can escalate; no per-edit oscillation or subagent spawn.
no JEV available -> deterministic path works, without any paid fallback.
malformed/unknown/missing/non-finite semantic answers cannot approve anything.
no semantic score overrides a required failure or grants destructive authority.
host-imported assessment carries matching request and evidence identity.
stale/ambiguous context IDs are rejected or regenerated.
meaningful source identifiers and project conventions remain intact.
clean-machine install discovers the entry skill and executes the correct prebuilt binary.
missing/corrupt/wrong-platform binary never falls back to compiling or fabricating success.
inactive hooks do no repository work; completion hook performs no long test run or model call.
stop-hook recursion, interruption and terminal incomplete are bounded.
active-session versions remain pinned; uninstall preserves project and unrelated data.
documented host syntax/capabilities match actually tested behavior.
no private fixtures, credentials, proprietary excerpts or raw pilot receipts are published.
inventory does not remove targets, worktrees or shared caches.
later cleanup removes only owned inactive regenerable resources within the allowed root.
changed identities, active resources, unique commits and ignored/untracked data are preserved.
disk reporting does not double-count shared paths; next-build cost is measured.
unknown usage/cost is null rather than zero; counters are not fabricated.
failed, incomplete and retried tasks remain in the benchmark denominator.
deferred work and final full checks remain in total cost; skipping is not passing.
